data.hook: Ashton Jeanty's ready to run, but Brock Bowers' knee procedure sidelines the Raiders' star tight end just before kickoff.
data.name: Raiders Get Jeanty Back but Rule Out Bowers for Dolphins Opener
data.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders cleared running back Ashton Jeanty from the injury report after his ankle recovery, setting him up for a full workload in Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET home opener against the Miami Dolphins at Allegiant Stadium. Star tight end Brock Bowers, however, is out following a Tuesday meniscus trim, with a possible Week 2 return against the Chargers. Both rebuild-mode teams start new head coaches and QBs—Kirk Cousins for Vegas under Klint Kubiak, Malik Willis for Miami with Jeff Hafley—while Dolphins are mostly healthy and former QB Ryan Fitzpatrick warns of a potential 0-17 season.

data.hook: Justin Herbert's rocket arm finally lets new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel dust off plays he couldn't call in Miami. Fans can't wait to see the sparks fly in the season opener.
data.name: Chargers Fans Eager for McDaniel's Unleashed Playbook with Herbert
data.summary: Mike McDaniel, hired by the Los Angeles Chargers in January after leaving the Dolphins, brings his motion-heavy scheme to pair with Herbert's elite arm talent. Analysts like Ian Rapoport note that Tua Tagovailoa's limitations in Miami kept certain downfield throws sidelined, but Herbert opens up the full playbook for explosive plays. The excitement builds as the Chargers host the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday at SoFi Stadium, their 2026 regular-season debut, with hopes Herbert could join the ranks of QBs with multiple 5,000-yard seasons.

data.hook: Brock Bowers, the Raiders' dynamic tight end, got a meniscus trim on his knee and will sit out Sunday's opener against Miami. The team hopes he'll be back the following week at the Chargers.
data.name: Raiders' Brock Bowers Out for Opener After Knee Procedure, Eye Week 2 Return
data.summary: The 23-year-old star had the minor procedure Tuesday after dealing with the knee issue since training camp. Backup Michael Mayer steps in for Week 1, fresh off a new contract and added bulk for the role. While the Raiders stay optimistic, fans and medical experts urge caution given Bowers' past knee injuries from last season and typical three-to-six week recoveries—many simply say 'LET HIM HEAL' to avoid risks.

data.hook: As the Chargers fell behind the Cardinals at SoFi Stadium, fans watching from home unleashed their frustration on offensive tackle Trey Pipkins, calling for him to come off the field right then and there.
data.name: Chargers Fans Blast Trey Pipkins After Week 1 Loss to Cardinals
data.summary: The Chargers lost 26-14 to the Arizona Cardinals in Week 1, despite being favored by nearly 10 points, with Justin Herbert throwing for 209 yards, one touchdown, and one interception while taking three sacks. Fans zeroed in on Trey Pipkins, a 2019 third-round pick serving as swing tackle, blaming him for at least one sack and questioning why he still gets playing time after years of perceived pass-protection struggles. Posts like "GET TREY PIPKINS OFF THE FUCKING FIELD" flooded feeds in real time, turning him into the main target of backlash over the team's uneven start.

data.name: Cardinals Stun Chargers 26-14 in Season Opener Behind Rookie TD
data.summary: The Arizona Cardinals pulled off a 26-14 upset over the favored Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, with new head coach Mike LaFleur notching his debut win—the first for a Cardinals coach since 1973. Rookie RB Jeremiyah Love scored on a 5-yard run, Jacoby Brissett threw a key TD to Trey McBride after a blocked punt, and Chad Ryland's field goals proved decisive. Justin Herbert passed for 209 yards and a TD to Ladd McConkey, but an interception and disjointed play left the Chargers searching for answers. Pop star Madison Beer, Herbert's fiancée, lit up the crowd with her visible reactions throughout the game.

data.hook: Myles Garrett pushed through knee pain in the Rams' opener but called it his worst game ever. Now, surgery means he'll miss at least four games.
data.name: Rams Place Myles Garrett on Injured Reserve After Knee Surgery
data.summary: The Rams acquired the two-time Defensive Player of the Year in a blockbuster offseason trade from the Cleveland Browns, but a lingering knee injury forced arthroscopic surgery. Garrett sat out most of training camp, struggled in the 27-7 season-opening loss to the 49ers in Australia with zero tackles or sacks, and now heads to injured reserve. He'll miss matchups against the Giants, Broncos, Eagles, and Bills, with a possible return in Week 6 against the Cardinals on Oct. 18. The team turns to edge rushers like Byron Young while awaiting Aaron Donald's impact.

data.hook: Empty stands gleam under SoFi's massive video board as fans snag Chargers opener tickets for as low as $24. It's a steal for Jim Harbaugh's home debut against the Cardinals.
data.name: Chargers Home Opener Tickets Drop to $24 at SoFi Stadium
data.summary: Secondary market prices for Sunday's 1:25 p.m. PT Chargers-Cardinals game at SoFi Stadium have plunged to $20-$35 for upper-level seats, with VIP packages dipping to $175 including parking. Fans mix excitement over the bargains with gripes about the matchup and sharing LA's sports spotlight with Dodgers, Lakers, and Rams. The low demand highlights Chargers' challenges in their shiny new home, though the stadium's ready with field setups and scoreboards for Harbaugh's era kickoff on CBS.
